subproblems.title: Tonelli sliding-window identity for left intervals
subproblems.statement: Let ν be an s-finite Borel measure on ℝ (for example any finite Borel measure) and let h ∈ ℝ. Then the function t ↦ ν((t − h, t)) from ℝ to [0, ∞] is Borel measurable. Its [0, ∞]-valued Lebesgue integral with respect to Lebesgue measure on ℝ is ∫⁻ ν((t − h, t)) dt = ENNReal.ofReal(h)·ν(ℝ). Here (t − h, t) = {x : t − h < x < t} is the open interval, which is empty when h ≤ 0, and ENNReal.ofReal(h) = max(h, 0) ∈ [0, ∞).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (ν : Measure ℝ) [SFinite ν] (h : ℝ), Measurable (fun t : ℝ => ν (Ioo (t - h) t)) ∧ ∫⁻ t, ν (Ioo (t - h) t) ∂volume = ENNReal.ofReal h * ν univ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent-supplied proof of cmc_fc_gs_ae_quotient_finite (Tonelli on the open set E_h). Here it is stated for an arbitrary s-finite measure ν and an arbitrary real h. Notation: Leb is Lebesgue measure on ℝ (Mathlib volume), ∫⁻ is the [0, ∞]-valued Lebesgue integral, and Leb ⊗ ν is the product measure on ℝ × ℝ (Mathlib volume.prod ν).

1. (The set E is measurable.) Let E := {(t, x) ∈ ℝ × ℝ : t − h < x and x < t}. Then E = A ∩ B with A := {p : p.1 − h < p.2} and B := {p : p.2 < p.1}. Each of A and B is the set where one measurable (indeed continuous) real function on ℝ × ℝ is strictly smaller than another. These functions are built from the projections p ↦ p.1 and p ↦ p.2 and subtraction of the constant h. So A and B are measurable (Mathlib measurableSet_lt), and hence so is E = A ∩ B.

2. (Sections of E.) Fix t ∈ ℝ. Then {x : (t, x) ∈ E} = {x : t − h < x < t} = (t − h, t), directly from the definition. Now fix x ∈ ℝ. Then {t : (t, x) ∈ E} = (x, x + h). Indeed t − h < x ⟺ t < x + h, so (t − h < x and x < t) ⟺ (x < t and t < x + h). Both directions are linear arithmetic.

3. (Measurability.) Since ν is s-finite and E is measurable, the function t ↦ ν({x : (t, x) ∈ E}) is measurable (Mathlib measurable_measure_prodMk_left, which needs only s-finiteness of ν). By step 2 this function is t ↦ ν((t − h, t)), which proves the first claim.

4. (Tonelli, integrating over t.) Since ν is s-finite and E is measurable, Mathlib Measure.prod_apply gives (Leb ⊗ ν)(E) = ∫⁻ ν({x : (t, x) ∈ E}) dt. By step 2 this equals ∫⁻ ν((t − h, t)) dt.

5. (Tonelli, integrating over x.) Leb is σ-finite, hence s-finite, and ν is s-finite. So Mathlib Measure.prod_apply_symm gives (Leb ⊗ ν)(E) = ∫⁻ Leb({t : (t, x) ∈ E}) dν(x). By step 2 this equals ∫⁻ Leb((x, x + h)) dν(x).

6. (Lebesgue measure of the sections.) For every x ∈ ℝ, Leb((x, x + h)) = ENNReal.ofReal((x + h) − x) = ENNReal.ofReal(h). This is Mathlib Real.volume_Ioo, valid for all real endpoints; when h ≤ 0 the interval is empty and both sides are 0. So the integrand in step 5 is the constant ENNReal.ofReal(h), and ∫⁻ ENNReal.ofReal(h) dν = ENNReal.ofReal(h)·ν(ℝ) (Mathlib lintegral_const).

7. (Conclusion.) Steps 4, 5 and 6 give ∫⁻ ν((t − h, t)) dt = (Leb ⊗ ν)(E) = ENNReal.ofReal(h)·ν(ℝ). This is the second claim; together with step 3 it proves the theorem. ∎
proof_key_steps: E := {(t, x) : t − h < x < t} is the intersection of two strict-inequality sets of measurable functions, so it is measurable (measurableSet_lt).
Sections: for fixed t, {x : (t, x) ∈ E} = (t − h, t); for fixed x, {t : (t, x) ∈ E} = (x, x + h).
Since ν is s-finite, t ↦ ν((t − h, t)) is measurable (measurable_measure_prodMk_left).
Tonelli in both orders (Measure.prod_apply, Measure.prod_apply_symm): ∫⁻ ν((t − h, t)) dt = (Leb ⊗ ν)(E) = ∫⁻ Leb((x, x + h)) dν(x).
Leb((x, x + h)) = ofReal(h) (Real.volume_Ioo), so the right side is ofReal(h)·ν(ℝ) (lintegral_const).

subproblems.title: Double Fatou: the iterated liminf of sequential left window quotients is finite a.e.
subproblems.statement: Let ν_j (j ∈ ℕ) be Borel measures on ℝ, and let Λ ∈ [0, ∞) satisfy ν_j(ℝ) ≤ Λ for every j. For j, n ∈ ℕ and t ∈ ℝ let Q_{j,n}(t) := (n + 1)·ν_j((t − 1/(n + 1), t)) ∈ [0, ∞]. Here n + 1 is read in [0, ∞] and 1/(n + 1) in ℝ. Then for Lebesgue-almost every t ∈ ℝ, liminf_{j→∞} liminf_{n→∞} Q_{j,n}(t) ≠ ∞. Both limits inferior are taken in [0, ∞] along atTop in ℕ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (ν : ℕ → Measure ℝ) (Λ : ℝ≥0∞), Λ ≠ ∞ → (∀ j, ν j univ ≤ Λ) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), liminf (fun j => liminf (fun n : ℕ => ((n : ℝ≥0∞) + 1) * ν j (Ioo (t - 1 / ((n : ℝ) + 1)) t)) atTop) atTop ≠ ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 3 and 4 of the parent-supplied proof of cmc_fc_gs_ae_quotient_finite (two applications of Fatou's lemma). Here it is stated for arbitrary measures ν_j with uniformly bounded total mass.

This proof uses the sibling lemma window_lintegral (Lean: Submission.cmc_fc_gs_aqf_window_lintegral). It says: for every s-finite Borel measure ν on ℝ and every h ∈ ℝ, the function t ↦ ν((t − h, t)) is measurable and ∫⁻ ν((t − h, t)) dt = ENNReal.ofReal(h)·ν(ℝ).

Notation is as in the statement. Leb is Lebesgue measure on ℝ, ∫⁻ is the [0, ∞]-valued Lebesgue integral with respect to Leb, and h_n := 1/(n + 1) ∈ ℝ.

1. (Finiteness.) For every j, ν_j(ℝ) ≤ Λ < ∞, so ν_j is a finite measure. In particular it is s-finite, so window_lintegral applies to ν_j.

2. (Q_{j,n} is measurable.) Fix j and n. By window_lintegral with ν := ν_j and h := h_n, the function t ↦ ν_j((t − h_n, t)) is measurable. Multiplying by the constant n + 1 ∈ [0, ∞] preserves measurability (Mathlib Measurable.const_mul). So Q_{j,n} is measurable.

3. (Normalization.) For every n ∈ ℕ, (n + 1)·ENNReal.ofReal(1/(n + 1)) = 1 in [0, ∞].
  Since n + 1 > 0 in ℝ and 1/(n + 1) = (n + 1)⁻¹, Mathlib ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos gives ENNReal.ofReal(1/(n + 1)) = (ENNReal.ofReal(n + 1))⁻¹.
  Next, ENNReal.ofReal(n + 1) = ENNReal.ofReal(n) + ENNReal.ofReal(1) = n + 1 in [0, ∞]. This uses ENNReal.ofReal_add (as n ≥ 0 and 1 ≥ 0), then ENNReal.ofReal_natCast and ENNReal.ofReal_one.
  The element n + 1 of [0, ∞] is neither 0 nor ∞, so (n + 1)·(n + 1)⁻¹ = 1 (ENNReal.mul_inv_cancel).

4. (Integral of Q_{j,n}.) By step 2 the function t ↦ ν_j((t − h_n, t)) is measurable, so the constant n + 1 can be pulled out of the integral (Mathlib lintegral_const_mul). With window_lintegral and step 3 this gives
  ∫⁻ Q_{j,n} = (n + 1)·∫⁻ ν_j((t − h_n, t)) dt = (n + 1)·(ENNReal.ofReal(h_n)·ν_j(ℝ)) = ((n + 1)·ENNReal.ofReal(h_n))·ν_j(ℝ) = ν_j(ℝ).

5. (First Fatou.) Let q_j(t) := liminf_{n→∞} Q_{j,n}(t). By step 2 and Mathlib Measurable.liminf, q_j is measurable. Fatou's lemma (Mathlib lintegral_liminf_le, with the measurability from step 2) and step 4 give
  ∫⁻ q_j ≤ liminf_{n→∞} ∫⁻ Q_{j,n} = liminf_{n→∞} ν_j(ℝ) = ν_j(ℝ) ≤ Λ.
  The liminf of a constant sequence is that constant (Filter.liminf_const; atTop on ℕ is a nontrivial filter).

6. (Second Fatou.) Let F(t) := liminf_{j→∞} q_j(t). By step 5 and Measurable.liminf, F is measurable. Fatou's lemma again (lintegral_liminf_le, with the measurability of the q_j) gives ∫⁻ F ≤ liminf_{j→∞} ∫⁻ q_j.
  By step 5, ∫⁻ q_j ≤ Λ for every j. So monotonicity of liminf (Filter.liminf_le_liminf) gives liminf_j ∫⁻ q_j ≤ liminf_j Λ = Λ, using Filter.liminf_const. No boundedness side conditions are needed, because [0, ∞] is a complete lattice.
  Hence ∫⁻ F ≤ Λ, and since Λ ≠ ∞, ∫⁻ F ≠ ∞.

7. (Finite almost everywhere.) A measurable [0, ∞]-valued function with finite integral is finite almost everywhere (Mathlib ae_lt_top). So F(t) < ∞, i.e. F(t) ≠ ∞, for Lebesgue-almost every t. Since F(t) = liminf_{j→∞} liminf_{n→∞} Q_{j,n}(t) is exactly the quantity in the statement, the theorem follows. ∎
proof_key_steps: Each ν_j has ν_j(ℝ) ≤ Λ < ∞, so it is finite, hence s-finite, and window_lintegral applies.
(n + 1)·ofReal(1/(n + 1)) = 1 in [0, ∞] (ofReal_inv_of_pos, ofReal_add, ofReal_natCast, mul_inv_cancel), so ∫⁻ Q_{j,n} = ν_j(ℝ) (lintegral_const_mul, window_lintegral).
First Fatou: q_j := liminf_n Q_{j,n} is measurable (Measurable.liminf) and ∫⁻ q_j ≤ liminf_n ν_j(ℝ) = ν_j(ℝ) ≤ Λ.
Second Fatou: F := liminf_j q_j is measurable and ∫⁻ F ≤ liminf_j ∫⁻ q_j ≤ Λ < ∞ (lintegral_liminf_le, liminf_le_liminf, liminf_const).
ae_lt_top: F(t) < ∞ for a.e. t, which is the claim.

subproblems.title: The lower left quotient is at most the sequential quotient of the restriction to [a, b]
subproblems.statement: Let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ, and let a, b, t ∈ ℝ with a < t < b. Put S(t) := liminf_{h→0+} ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ((t − h, t)) ∈ [0, ∞], the limit inferior in [0, ∞] along the filter 𝓝[>] 0. Let μ⌞[a, b] be the restriction of μ to [a, b], i.e. (μ⌞[a, b])(E) = μ(E ∩ [a, b]) for Borel E. Then S(t) ≤ liminf_{n→∞} (n + 1)·(μ⌞[a, b])((t − 1/(n + 1), t)). The right side is a limit inferior in [0, ∞] along atTop in ℕ, with n + 1 read in [0, ∞] and 1/(n + 1) in ℝ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (μ : Measure ℝ) (a b t : ℝ), t ∈ Ioo a b → liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ (Ioo (t - h) t)) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ liminf (fun n : ℕ => ((n : ℝ≥0∞) + 1) * (μ.restrict (Icc a b)) (Ioo (t - 1 / ((n : ℝ) + 1)) t)) atTop
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent-supplied proof of cmc_fc_gs_ae_quotient_finite (the comparison S_j ≤ q_j on (a, b)), here for a single measure μ. No finiteness of μ is needed.

1. (The sequence h_n.) For n ∈ ℕ let h_n := 1/(n + 1) ∈ ℝ. Then h_n → 0 as n → ∞ (Mathlib tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat), and h_n > 0, i.e. h_n ∈ (0, ∞), for every n. Hence h_n → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0 = 𝓝[(0, ∞)] 0 (Mathlib tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff: convergence in 𝓝 0 together with eventual membership in (0, ∞)).

2. (Filter liminf versus sequential liminf.) For h ∈ ℝ let u(h) := ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ((t − h, t)), so S(t) is the liminf of u along 𝓝[>] 0. Since h_n → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0, Mathlib Filter.Tendsto.liminf_le_liminf_comp gives liminf_{𝓝[>] 0} u ≤ liminf_{n→∞} u(h_n). Its boundedness side conditions hold automatically because [0, ∞] is a complete lattice. So S(t) ≤ liminf_n ENNReal.ofReal(h_n⁻¹)·μ((t − h_n, t)).

3. (The window eventually lies in [a, b].) Since t − a > 0 and h_n → 0 in ℝ, there is N with h_n < t − a for all n ≥ N (Mathlib tendsto_order). Fix such an n. If t − h_n < x < t, then x > t − h_n > a and x < t < b, so x ∈ [a, b]. Thus (t − h_n, t) ⊆ [a, b]. The open interval is Borel, so (μ⌞[a, b])((t − h_n, t)) = μ((t − h_n, t) ∩ [a, b]) = μ((t − h_n, t)) (Mathlib Measure.restrict_apply, then Set.inter_eq_left).

4. (The normalizing factor.) For every n, h_n⁻¹ = (1/(n + 1))⁻¹ = n + 1 in ℝ. Also ENNReal.ofReal(n + 1) = ENNReal.ofReal(n) + ENNReal.ofReal(1) = n + 1 in [0, ∞] (ENNReal.ofReal_add with n ≥ 0 and 1 ≥ 0, then ENNReal.ofReal_natCast and ENNReal.ofReal_one). So ENNReal.ofReal(h_n⁻¹) = n + 1.

5. (Eventual equality.) By steps 3 and 4, for every n ≥ N, u(h_n) = ENNReal.ofReal(h_n⁻¹)·μ((t − h_n, t)) = (n + 1)·(μ⌞[a, b])((t − h_n, t)). A liminf along atTop depends only on eventual values (Mathlib Filter.liminf_congr). So liminf_n u(h_n) = liminf_n (n + 1)·(μ⌞[a, b])((t − h_n, t)).

6. (Conclusion.) By steps 2 and 5, S(t) ≤ liminf_n (n + 1)·(μ⌞[a, b])((t − 1/(n + 1), t)). ∎
proof_key_steps: h_n = 1/(n + 1) → 0 through positive values, so h_n → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0 (tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat, tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff).
Filter.Tendsto.liminf_le_liminf_comp: the liminf along 𝓝[>] 0 of u(h) = ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ((t − h, t)) is at most liminf_n u(h_n).
Eventually h_n < t − a, so (t − h_n, t) ⊆ [a, b] and μ((t − h_n, t)) = (μ⌞[a, b])((t − h_n, t)) (tendsto_order, Measure.restrict_apply).
ofReal(h_n⁻¹) = n + 1 in [0, ∞], so u(h_n) eventually equals (n + 1)·(μ⌞[a, b])((t − h_n, t)), and liminf_congr finishes the proof.
